builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CoSTA: Co-Evolving Self-Play Timeline Agents for Complex Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering
summary: Replaces single-context TKGQA reasoning with a coordinator-worker architecture that delegates temporal evidence gathering to specialized agents. Requires training infrastructure for role-conditioned distillation and co-evolving self-play optimization, plus runtime orchestration overhead. Performance depends on effective learned collaboration; if coordination fails or evidence synthesis degrades, answer quality may not exceed simpler single-agent or retrieval approaches.
rationale: While the multi-agent architecture is conceptually applicable to constrained settings via API-based agents, the method requires self-play training and distillation infrastructure that exceeds a 24GB GPU budget, and the actual deployment cost and latency of the coordinator-worker pattern are not quantified.

claims.statement: Replaces single-context TKGQA reasoning with a coordinator-worker architecture that delegates temporal evidence gathering to specialized agents. Requires training infrastructure for role-conditioned distillation and co-evolving self-play optimization, plus runtime orchestration overhead. Performance depends on effective learned collaboration; if coordination fails or evidence synthesis degrades, answer quality may not exceed simpler single-agent or retrieval approaches.

Achieves state-of-the-art overall performance across three TKGQA benchmarks, with strong gains on complex multi-fact questions; compact variants outperform evaluated closed-source LLM agents. No multiplicative factor reported.
